accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS 2024 framework (Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning: active learning, keep on trying; ELG Fine Motor Skills: scissors, pencils and cutlery with growing accuracy) and Development Matters 2021 (3 and 4 year olds persist with activities; Reception resilience and perseverance). The little-and-often claim follows the distributed practice effect (Cepeda et al. 2006 meta-analysis; Shea et al. 2000 on motor skill retention), and the lab model keeps total practice equal (5 short goes against 1 long go) so the comparison is fair. Praise for effort rather than talent follows Mueller and Dweck 1998.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented beliefs that block practice in young children: ability is fixed or inborn (prediction on Then and now, tags born and luck), giving up after a wobbly first try (prediction Just as wobbly or Worse, tag quit), relying on others instead of trying (tag others), cramming in one long go (prediction and tag cram), practising only the easy parts (prediction A and M again, tag easy), watching instead of doing (tag watch), and crediting the tool rather than practice (tag tool).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagprac is a practice simulator: the cut line's wobble shrinks by a fixed factor with each go so the child sees go 1, 2 and 3 overlaid, the then-and-now pairs draw the same skill at two practice levels, a bar chart races 5 short goes against 1 long go, and a name has a per-letter neatness the child raises only by practising that letter. flagstick (sticking with it), flagoops and flagswap are about finishing, mistakes and changing strategy, with no repetition model; the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule before reading it: their own three cuts get visibly closer to the dotted line with stars rising, the chart shows the daily plan climbing to 80 percent while the one-long-go bars slip back, and tapping the neat A or M does nothing (A is already neat) while tapping S makes the whole name neat. Done messages name the idea only after the evidence is on screen.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: Just as wobbly or Worse for the third cut (it is neater), They were just born good (every later try in the pairs was the practised one), One long go on Monday (its bars slip back by Friday), and A and M again (practising them is refused because they are already neat). A.reveal repeats the child's own guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each naming the slip: quit (a wobbly go is not a reason to stop), others (if you never try it never gets easier for you), cram (one long go helps for a day, then it slips), watch (your legs learn by doing), easy (practise the part still wobbly), luck and born (everyone starts wobbly; that was practice), tool (same pencil, more practice) and always (your first tries were wobbly).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences (The first time you cut with scissors, the line is wobbly. That is fine.) and pass the family kid limit; the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences to pass the adult limit while keeping the exact terms: Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning, active learning, persistence, fine motor skills, spaced or distributed practice, massed practice and automatic.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and overlap with every lesson, including Persisting when it's hard, Having a go at something new and Sticking with it, is under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (first tries are wobbly, repeat, little and often, the tricky bit and comparing tries); the adult paragraphs give the framework statements, the key words, four named mistakes with the praise caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the wiggly line spans the canvas width with the scissors at the start, the two then-and-now cards are about 110 px wide with Try A and Try B labels, the two bar charts fit side by side with readable M to F labels and Friday percentages, and every action has a 56 px button twin (Cut along the line, Try A came later, Practise S, Practise today). Nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Every canvas drag or tap has a labelled button, the canvas aria-label speaks each result (Go 2: two stars. Neater than before!), and states use words and stars (wobbly, neat, 3 of 5 days), not colour alone.
